objects.definition:
typedef struct {
  WORD32 sample_rate;               /* audio file sample rate */
  WORD32 bitrate;                   /* encoder bit rate in bits/sec */
  WORD32 num_channels_in;           /* number of channels on input (1,2) */
  WORD32 num_channels_out;          /* number of channels on output (1,2) */
  WORD32 bandwidth;                 /* targeted audio bandwidth in Hz */
  WORD32 dual_mono;                 /* flag: make 2 SCEs for stereo input files */
  WORD32 use_tns;                   /* flag: use temporal noise shaping */
  WORD32 noise_filling;             /* flag: use noise filling */
  WORD32 use_adts;                  /* flag: use ADTS instead of ADIF */
  WORD32 private_bit;               /* private bit of MPEG Header */
  WORD32 copyright_bit;             /* copyright bit of MPEG Header */
  WORD32 original_copy_bit;         /* original bit of MPEG Header */
  WORD32 f_no_stereo_preprocessing; /* forbid usage of stereo prerpocessing */
  WORD32 inv_quant;                 /* improve distortion by inverse quantization */
  WORD32 full_bandwidth;            /* improve distortion by inverse quantization */
  WORD32 bitreservoir_size;         /* size of bit reservoir (default:0; max 6144)*/
  WORD32 length;
} ixheaace_aac_enc_config;
objects.description: AAC-specific encoder configuration parameters such as sample rate, bitrate, channels, tools and header flags. Consumed as a sub-config within broader input configuration.

Top-level encoder input configuration specifying sample format, bitrate, channel layout, codec mode (AAC/USAC variants), SBR/ESBR/MPS options, DRC, loudness metadata, and embedded AAC-specific config. Passed into creation/processing APIs.
Holds pointers to library name and version strings returned by the encoder library.
Output/control structure populated by the encoder: I/O byte counts, memory bookkeeping, proc object handle, custom allocators, version info, memory tables, stream parameters and flags.
Convenience aggregate bundling input and output configuration for the encoder API.
Minimal input configuration holding only codec_mode. Likely used for a simplified or alternative API path.

functions.name: ixheaacd_get_lib_id_strings
functions.description: Populates library identification strings for this component. The function writes library metadata (likely name and version) into the output structure provided by the caller. Based on nearby declarations, pv_output is expected to reference an ia_lib_info_struct whose fields (p_lib_name, p_version_num) will be set to point to the library’s identifier strings. Usage: allocate an ia_lib_info_struct, pass its address as pv_output, then read the name/version pointers populated by the function. Details such as ownership/lifetime of the returned strings and thread-safety are not documented and are assumed to be static or internally managed. Unknowns: exact type expected for pv_output is inferred (ia_lib_info_struct) and not explicitly documented here; error behavior is unspecified since the function returns VOID.
requirements: pv_output must be a non-NULL, writable pointer.
pv_output should point to a valid, properly sized ia_lib_info_struct instance (inferred from the adjacent typedef).
The memory referenced by pv_output must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Callers should not attempt to free or modify the strings referenced by p_lib_name and p_version_num unless explicitly documented elsewhere (inferred; likely static strings).
No return value or explicit error reporting is provided; callers cannot detect failure from this API alone.

functions.name: ixheaace_get_lib_id_strings
functions.description: Returns the encoder library identification strings (library name and version). Call it to query versioning information for logging/diagnostics before creating/using the encoder. The function writes results to the structure passed via pv_output, which, based on the header, is expected to be an ixheaace_version containing pointers to the name and version strings.
requirements: pv_output must be a valid, non-null pointer.
pv_output should point to an ixheaace_version instance large enough to receive the name and version pointers.
The returned name/version pointers are likely library-owned/static; the caller should not free or modify them (inferred from typical library pattern and pointer fields in ixheaace_version).
The caller must check the returned IA_ERRORCODE and handle non-success values appropriately.
Thread-safety/recursion guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: ixheaace_create
functions.description: Handles encoder memory requirements and performs initialization. Typically used to configure the encoder instance (codec mode, sample rate, channels, bitrates, and internal memory tables) and to return any opaque encoder object/context and buffers needed for processing.
requirements: pv_input must be a valid, non-null pointer. It is expected to reference configuration data for the encoder. Based on the header, this is likely either ixheaace_input_config or ixheaace_user_config_struct (unknown which is required).

pv_output must be a valid, non-null pointer. It is expected to reference an output/config structure that the function will populate (e.g., memory tables, encoder object handle). Based on the header, this likely relates to ixheaace_output_config within ixheaace_user_config_struct (exact layout unknown).
All configuration fields required by the encoder must be initialized before calling (specific required fields are not documented here; unknown).
The caller must check the returned IA_ERRORCODE and not proceed to processing on failure.
Must be called before ixheaace_process and ixheaace_delete on the same instance.
Ownership and lifetime of any memory callbacks or pointers provided via pv_input/pv_output must remain valid for the duration of the encoder instance (inferred).

functions.name: ixheaace_process
functions.signature: IA_ERRORCODE ixheaace_process(pVOID pv_ia_process_api_obj, pVOID pstr_in_cfg, pVOID pstr_out_cfg);
functions.description: Encodes one input frame. Uses the initialized encoder instance to consume input samples and produce encoded output bytes and accounting (bytes consumed/produced, etc.). Input and output frame configuration are passed via opaque pointers.
requirements: pv_ia_process_api_obj must be a valid, non-null encoder instance/object obtained and initialized via ixheaace_create.
pstr_in_cfg must be a valid, non-null pointer to the input frame configuration/buffer descriptor expected by the encoder (exact structure type is not specified here; unknown).

pstr_out_cfg must be a valid, non-null pointer to an output/result descriptor that will be filled by the encoder (e.g., number of bytes produced, buffer pointer/size). Exact structure type is unspecified; unknown.
Must be called only after a successful ixheaace_create for the corresponding encoder instance.
Input buffers referenced in pstr_in_cfg must contain enough PCM data for the configured frame length and must remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred).
Output buffers referenced in pstr_out_cfg must be allocated with sufficient capacity to hold the encoded frame (capacity requirement unknown; caller must check produced size).
The caller must check IA_ERRORCODE on return and handle errors. Do not reuse or advance buffers on failure unless explicitly handled by the API (policy unknown).

functions.name: ixheaace_delete
functions.description: Releases/frees all allocated resources for the encoder instance. Call when the encoder is no longer needed to avoid memory leaks.
requirements: pv_output must be a valid, non-null pointer to the encoder’s output/config context that holds allocation info for cleanup (exact structure type is not specified here; likely relates to ixheaace_output_config; unknown).
Must be called after ixheaace_create and after finishing all ixheaace_process calls for the instance.
Must not be called more than once for the same instance/context (inferred).
After successful deletion, the encoder instance/object and any associated pointers must not be used again.
The caller must check IA_ERRORCODE and treat non-success as a failure to fully release resources.
